topic.meaning: The sentence states a decision (ship quickly) together with its explicit cost (deferred soak test).
topic.grammarUsage: "shipped the fix in under an hour" uses past tense + in + under + time; "but the trade-off is that ..." frames the cost as a named consequence.
topic.nuance: "shipped" emphasizes release completion; "in under an hour" adds speed pride; "trade-off" keeps the decision honest.
topic.differenceFromSimilar: "shipped the fix" includes release; "hotfixed" implies urgency/patch; "skipped testing" foregrounds risk rather than decision.
topic.alternativeExample: Alternative: "We merged the patch before dinner, but the downside is that monitoring coverage is thin."
